summary: The batch substantially implements S5 and all reported gates pass, but it is not ready. A confirmed S3 policy error rejects the headerless presigned uploads used by the application, production can silently inherit synthetic audio-retention values despite the unresolved production policy, and required live recovery/security acceptance evidence remains pending. The implementation guide itself was unchanged from HEAD.
substeps_covered: Prerequisites — complete for code review: S4 supplies private database placement/security groups and the S3 gateway interface; S0 adopted the synthetic staging defaults. Production retention remains unresolved in the deployment contract.

S5.1 RDS provisioning — partial: PostgreSQL 16, db.t4g.small, single-AZ staging, 50 GiB gp3, capped autoscaling, scheduled maintenance/backups, encryption, deletion protection, and final snapshots are configured. Regional class/storage availability and an exact supported minor remain unverified.

S5.2 backups/recovery — partial: staging uses seven days and production requires an explicit database-backup decision. LatestRestorableTime and actual backup availability have not been verified because nothing has been applied.
S5.3 database TLS — complete in configuration: rds.force_ssl=1 is attached, and existing clients use verify-full with CA/hostname verification. Rotation guidance is documented.

S5.4 audio bucket — incorrect: public-access blocks, owner-enforced ownership, versioning, SSE-KMS defaults, Bucket Keys, and TLS policies exist, but the encryption-header deny conditions also deny requests with absent SSE headers, breaking the current presign contract.

S5.5 lifecycle — complete for synthetic staging: separate current/noncurrent expiry and multipart cleanup exist, with no archive transition or Object Lock. Production values are unsafe because unresolved policy defaults to staging's seven days.
S5.6 overwrite race — complete as an explicit deferral: documentation accurately states versioning is not immutability and requires version/checksum binding before PHI use in Step 9.

S5.7 queues — complete in default environment configuration: one standard queue plus DLQ, 300-second visibility, 20-second long polling, maxReceiveCount=3, 4/14-day retention, source-restricted redrive, SSE-KMS, and insecure-transport denies are present. Operator IAM remains correctly assigned to S6.

S5.8 key/data-copy boundaries — complete in design: application data uses a distinct rotating KMS key, security-log storage is not conflated with audio, and unrecoverability plus retained-copy implications are documented.
S5.9 exports — complete: no unsupported application export bucket was introduced.

Integration/later steps — complete at interface level: foundation manifests expose bucket, queue, database, and key identifiers; release roots require the application-facing values; S6/S8/S9/Step 9 obligations are documented without prematurely adding their resources.

HIPAA-focused review — no new authentication, session, tenant-isolation, URL, logging, or application authorization code was introduced. Confirmed findings concern storage availability and retention below; least-privilege runtime enforcement remains pending S6 and must not be treated as compliance evidence.
Validation — fmt, clippy, test, tf-manifest, and tf-network reportedly pass. Mock tests mostly inspect Terraform structure; they do not establish live AWS behavior, recovery, or HIPAA compliance.

blockers.problem: Confirmed availability defect: both PutObject deny statements use StringNotEqualsIfExists. In an explicit Deny with a negated IfExists operator, a missing condition key still satisfies the deny. The application's presigner sends only Content-Type (crates/er-server/src/routes.rs:286), so ordinary headerless uploads are denied instead of receiving bucket-default SSE-KMS. This breaks every audio-upload workflow. The test at infra/modules/data/tests/data.tftest.hcl:115 merely asserts the mistaken policy shape and therefore validates the opposite of externally meaningful behavior.
blockers.required_fix: Express each wrong-header denial so it applies only when that header is present, for example by combining an appropriate Null condition with StringNotEquals, while allowing both SSE headers to be absent. Add a behavioral/live policy test proving a current headerless presigned PUT succeeds and wrong algorithm/key requests fail.

blockers.problem: Confirmed retention/data-loss risk: production defaults current and noncurrent audio retention to the synthetic seven-day values, while validation only requires explicit database availability and backup decisions. Thus the example production configuration at infra/envs/prod/foundation/terraform.tfvars.example:30 can be enabled and automatically expire production audio under an unapproved policy. This contradicts the comment at lines 118-119 and the unresolved production retention/hold requirement at docs/ops/deployment-contract.md:45.
blockers.required_fix: Require explicit production audio current-version and noncurrent-version retention decisions before enabled=true, sourced from the approved production retention/hold policy. Update the example and tests to prove production enablement fails when those decisions are omitted.

blockers.problem: S5 acceptance remains unverifiable: the document records regional RDS class/storage and minor-version verification, applied-resource inspection, LatestRestorableTime, signed upload behavior, object encryption metadata, and runtime-role negative checks as pending. It also states that no database, bucket, queue, or key has been applied. Therefore the guide's cloud-inspection acceptance criteria are not yet satisfied despite the offline gates passing.
blockers.required_fix: After correcting the policy and completing the dependent S6 permissions, apply to the approved synthetic staging account and record the required cloud/API evidence: supported RDS combination/minor, private/encrypted resources, advancing restore time, successful headerless signed upload, rejected public/insecure/wrong-encryption requests, expected object KMS metadata, queue/DLQ settings, and negative runtime-role control mutations.
